navigate.name: Go to page
navigate.description: Send a control surface to one of its pages. The grid animates exactly as if the pad had been pressed, growing out of wherever that page sits on the screen it is leaving — that is not an invented origin, it is the pad a finger would have used. What actually caused the move is carried on the event instead, where an automation needs it and the grid cannot say it.

init.title: What each colour means
init.description:
A pad shows its colour when the thing behind it is **on**, and **white** when it is off. That is the one rule the grid cannot bend, so white is not on offer here.

The device has five colours and that is all it has, so this asks what each one means rather than asking after each kind of thing one at a time. **Every kind of thing belongs in exactly one box.** To paint your lights green, take them out of orange and put them in green — and you will see what they were sharing orange with.

Purple only takes things with no on and off of their own. Purple against white is the one pair too close to tell apart on this hardware, so on anything that can be switched off it would be unreadable exactly when it mattered.

data_description.orange: The usual home for anything with a plain on and off.
data_description.green: Openings, and the things a pad only watches.
data_description.purple: Only things you press once, which never show white.

error.colour_twice: {kinds} — in two boxes at once. Every kind of thing has exactly one colour, so take it out of the one you did not mean.
error.colour_missing: {kinds} — not in any box. Every kind of thing needs a colour, or its pads would have nothing to show.
error.purple_needs_stateless: {kinds} — cannot be purple, because they can be switched off and so show white when they are. Purple and white are the one pair too close to tell apart on this device, which would make them unreadable exactly when it mattered.

user.title: Add a page
user.description:
A page is one screen of sixteen pads. Give it a room and it fills itself from what is in that room; give it a label and it fills itself from whatever carries that label, across rooms; give it neither and it is yours to fill pad by pad.

The colour names it on the first screen, and it is the curtain that sweeps across when you go in and out.

reconfigure.description:
A page is one screen of sixteen pads. Give it a room and it fills itself from what is in that room; give it a label and it fills itself from whatever carries that label, across rooms; give it neither and it is yours to fill pad by pad.

The colour names it on the first screen, and it is the curtain that sweeps across when you go in and out.

pads.title: Pin things to pads
pads.description:
Sixteen pads, counted the way you read them:

```
{grid}
```

The fields below are filled in with **what this page shows right now**, so you can see it and change any of it. Only what you actually change is stored: leave one as it is and that pad carries on filling itself from the page's room or label, so looking at a page and saving it does not quietly freeze it.

Clear a field and the pad goes back to being filled from the room. On a page with no room at all, these are the whole page.

What a pad *does* still comes from what is behind it — a lamp toggles, a scene runs, and holding anything a knob can adjust points the knobs at it.

A pad may also be a **readout**. Pin a door sensor or a person and it shows you rather than offering you: its colour when the door is open or the person is in, white when not, and a shudder if you press it. What is never offered is anything the grid cannot show — a temperature has no on and no off, and a pad that sat white forever would be lying about it.

error.one_source: A page fills itself from one place. Choose a room or a label, not both.
